title: Great Ruler of All Nature's Frame
description: Great Ruler of All Nature's Frame in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 546, “God Tempers the Wind to the Shorn Lamb”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Great ru-ler of all na-ture's frame, We own Thy power di-vine; We hear Thy breath in ev-ery storm, For all the winds are Thine.

lines: Great ruler of all nature's frame,
We hear Thy breath in every storm,
For all the winds are Thine.
Wide as they sweep their sounding way,
And awed by Thy majestic voice,
To those who seek Thy face;
And mingles with the tempest's roar
Those gentle whispers let me hear,
And gales of Paradise shall lull

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
